title: Quality control of oceanographic in situ data from Argo floats using climatological convex hulls
author: Udaya Bhaskar, Venkat Shesu, et al.

steps.title: Download climatology data
steps.instruction: Obtain the quality‑controlled climatological salinity data for the profiling depth of interest (2000 m) from the World Ocean Database 2013 (WOD13).

steps.title: Extract depth‑specific values
steps.instruction: From the WOD13 dataset, extract salinity observations that correspond to the chosen profiling depth (2000 m) together with their geographic coordinates (longitude and latitude).

steps.title: Build convex hull
steps.instruction: Construct an n‑sided convex‑hull polygon for each float location using the Jarvis March algorithm applied to the extracted (longitude, salinity) and (latitude, salinity) pairs.

steps.title: Retrieve Argo float data
steps.instruction: Download the Argo float salinity time series for the same profiling depth (2000 m) for the float(s) to be evaluated.

steps.title: Test points against polygon
steps.instruction: For every profile, apply a point‑in‑polygon (PIP) algorithm to determine whether the salinity point (with its longitude and latitude) lies inside the previously built convex‑hull polygon.

steps.title: Flag anomalous profiles
steps.instruction: Mark any profile whose salinity point falls outside the polygon as suspect (possible drift, offset, spike, or genuine anomalous oceanic condition).

steps.title: Optional visualization
steps.instruction: Plot the convex‑hull polygon in longitude‑salinity and latitude‑salinity space, overlay the Argo trajectory and highlight flagged profiles for visual inspection.
